import functools
import importlib
import inspect
import logging
import os
import time
import types
from pathlib import Path
from functools import singledispatch

import numpy as np
import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp


logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

TOPS_CPU_FALLBACK = "TOPS_CPU_FALLBACK"
TOPS_DUMP_DIR = "TOPS_DUMP_DIR"
TOPS_DUMP_INCLUDE = "TOPS_DUMP_INCLUDE"
TOPS_DUMP_EXCLUDE = "TOPS_DUMP_EXCLUDE"

_GLOBAL_ENABLE_TOKENS = {"1", "true", "all", "*"}
_UNRESOLVED = object()
_TRACER_FALLBACK_WARNED: set[str] = set()


def _env_tokens(name: str) -> set[str]:
  value = os.environ.get(name, "")
  return {token.strip().lower() for token in value.split(",") if token.strip()}


def _export_fn_name(fn) -> str:
  return getattr(fn, "__name__", fn.__class__.__name__)


def _export_qualified_name(fn) -> str:
  module = getattr(fn, "__module__", "")
  name = _export_fn_name(fn)
  return f"{module}.{name}" if module else name


def _matches_export_filter(tokens: set[str], fn) -> bool:
  if not tokens:
    return False
  if tokens & _GLOBAL_ENABLE_TOKENS:
    return True
  fn_name = _export_fn_name(fn).lower()
  qualified_name = _export_qualified_name(fn).lower()
  module_name = getattr(fn, "__module__", "").lower()
  return fn_name in tokens or qualified_name in tokens or module_name in tokens


def _should_fallback(fn) -> bool:
  return _matches_export_filter(_env_tokens(TOPS_CPU_FALLBACK), fn)


def _should_dump(fn) -> bool:
  if not os.environ.get(TOPS_DUMP_DIR):
    return False

  include = _env_tokens(TOPS_DUMP_INCLUDE)
  exclude = _env_tokens(TOPS_DUMP_EXCLUDE)

  if include and not _matches_export_filter(include, fn):
    return False
  return not _matches_export_filter(exclude, fn)


def _contains_tracer(value) -> bool:
  try:
    leaves = jax.tree_util.tree_leaves(value)
  except Exception:
    leaves = (value,)
  return any(isinstance(leaf, jax.core.Tracer) for leaf in leaves)


def _is_concrete_array(value) -> bool:
  return isinstance(value, jax.Array) and not isinstance(value, jax.core.Tracer)


def _get_original_device(value):
  if _is_concrete_array(value):
    return list(value.devices())[0]
  if isinstance(value, dict):
    values = value.values()
  elif isinstance(value, (list, tuple)):
    values = value
  else:
    return None

  for item in values:
    device = _get_original_device(item)
    if device is not None:
      return device
  return None


def _move_value_to_device(value, device):
  if _is_concrete_array(value):
    return jax.device_put(value, device)
  if isinstance(value, tuple):
    return tuple(_move_value_to_device(item, device) for item in value)
  if isinstance(value, list):
    return [_move_value_to_device(item, device) for item in value]
  if isinstance(value, dict):
    return {key: _move_value_to_device(item, device) for key, item in value.items()}
  return value


def _move_args_to_device(args, kwargs, device):
  return (
    tuple(_move_value_to_device(arg, device) for arg in args),
    {key: _move_value_to_device(value, device) for key, value in kwargs.items()},
  )


def _move_result_to_device(result, device):
  return _move_value_to_device(result, device)


def _dump_value(value):
  if value is None:
    return None
  if isinstance(value, jax.Array):
    return np.asarray(value)
  if isinstance(value, np.ndarray):
    return value
  if isinstance(value, (str, bytes, int, float, bool, np.number)):
    return value
  if isinstance(value, tuple):
    return tuple(_dump_value(item) for item in value)
  if isinstance(value, list):
    return [_dump_value(item) for item in value]
  if isinstance(value, dict):
    return {key: _dump_value(item) for key, item in value.items()}
  return value


def _shape_of(value):
  shape = getattr(value, "shape", None)
  return tuple(shape) if shape is not None else None


def _dtype_of(value):
  dtype = getattr(value, "dtype", None)
  return str(dtype) if dtype is not None else None


def _as_output_items(result):
  if isinstance(result, tuple):
    return result
  return (result,)


def _collect_input_dump(fn, args, kwargs):
  if _contains_tracer((args, kwargs)):
    return None

  signature = inspect.signature(fn)
  bound = signature.bind_partial(*args, **kwargs)
  inputs = {name: _dump_value(value) for name, value in bound.arguments.items()}
  return {
    "inputs": inputs,
    "input_shapes": {name: _shape_of(value) for name, value in bound.arguments.items()},
    "input_dtypes": {name: _dtype_of(value) for name, value in bound.arguments.items()},
    "timestamp": time.time(),
  }


def _flush_dump(fn, pending, result):
  if pending is None or _contains_tracer(result):
    return

  dump_dir = Path(os.environ[TOPS_DUMP_DIR])
  dump_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

  timestamp = pending["timestamp"]
  output_items = _as_output_items(result)
  outputs = {
    str(idx): _dump_value(value) for idx, value in enumerate(output_items)
  }
  meta = {
    "fn": _export_qualified_name(fn),
    "shapes": pending["input_shapes"],
    "dtypes": pending["input_dtypes"],
    "output_shapes": {
      str(idx): _shape_of(value) for idx, value in enumerate(output_items)
    },
    "output_dtypes": {
      str(idx): _dtype_of(value) for idx, value in enumerate(output_items)
    },
    "timestamp": timestamp,
    "pid": os.getpid(),
  }
  filename = f"{_export_qualified_name(fn)}_{timestamp:.6f}_rank{os.getpid()}.npz"
  path = dump_dir / filename
  np.savez(
    path,
    inputs=np.array(pending["inputs"], dtype=object),
    outputs=np.array(outputs, dtype=object),
    meta=np.array(meta, dtype=object),
  )


def _resolve_cpu_impl(fn, cpu_impl):
  if cpu_impl is not None:
    return cpu_impl

  module_path = getattr(fn, "__module__", "")
  if not module_path.startswith("tops.ops."):
    raise ModuleNotFoundError(
      f"Cannot infer CPU implementation for non-ops module {module_path!r}."
    )

  cpu_module_path = module_path.replace("tops.ops.", "tops.cpu.ops.", 1)
  cpu_module = importlib.import_module(cpu_module_path)
  return getattr(cpu_module, _export_fn_name(fn))


class _ExportedFunction:
  def __init__(self, fn, cpu_impl=None):
    self._fn = fn
    self._cpu_impl = cpu_impl
    self._resolved_cpu_impl = _UNRESOLVED
    functools.update_wrapper(self, fn)
    try:
      self.__signature__ = inspect.signature(fn)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
      pass

  def __getattr__(self, name):
    return getattr(self._fn, name)

  def __call__(self, *args, **kwargs):
    pending_dump = None
    if _should_dump(self._fn):
      try:
        pending_dump = _collect_input_dump(self._fn, args, kwargs)
      except Exception as exc:
        logger.warning(
          "Failed to collect dump inputs for %s: %s",
          _export_qualified_name(self._fn),
          exc,
        )

    if _should_fallback(self._fn):
      try:
        if _contains_tracer((args, kwargs)):
          fn_name = _export_qualified_name(self._fn)
          if fn_name not in _TRACER_FALLBACK_WARNED:
            _TRACER_FALLBACK_WARNED.add(fn_name)
            logger.warning(
              "CPU fallback skipped for %s under JAX tracing; "
              "fallback is eager-only. Running original implementation.",
              fn_name,
            )
          result = self._fn(*args, **kwargs)
        else:
          if self._resolved_cpu_impl is _UNRESOLVED:
            self._resolved_cpu_impl = _resolve_cpu_impl(self._fn, self._cpu_impl)

          original_device = _get_original_device((args, kwargs))
          cpu = jax.devices("cpu")[0]
          cpu_args, cpu_kwargs = _move_args_to_device(args, kwargs, cpu)
          with jax.default_device(cpu):
            result = self._resolved_cpu_impl(*cpu_args, **cpu_kwargs)
          if original_device is not None and original_device != cpu:
            result = _move_result_to_device(result, original_device)
      except Exception as exc:
        logger.warning(
          "CPU fallback failed for %s; running original implementation: %s",
          _export_qualified_name(self._fn),
          exc,
        )
        result = self._fn(*args, **kwargs)
    else:
      result = self._fn(*args, **kwargs)

    if pending_dump is not None:
      try:
        _flush_dump(self._fn, pending_dump, result)
      except Exception as exc:
        logger.warning(
          "Failed to dump I/O for %s: %s",
          _export_qualified_name(self._fn),
          exc,
        )

    return result


def export(fn=None, *, cpu_impl=None):
  """Mark a public kernel API for runtime CPU fallback and I/O dump.

  Args:
      fn: Function being decorated.
      cpu_impl: Optional CPU reference implementation. If omitted, the
          implementation is inferred by replacing ``tops.ops.`` with
          ``tops.cpu.ops.`` in the decorated function's module path.

  Returns:
      Callable wrapper preserving the original signature and forwarding
      attributes such as ``custom_vjp.defvjp`` to the wrapped object.
  """

  def decorate(inner_fn):
    return _ExportedFunction(inner_fn, cpu_impl=cpu_impl)

  if fn is None:
    return decorate
  return decorate(fn)


def next_power_of_2(n: int):
  """Return the smallest power of 2 greater than or equal to n"""
  n -= 1
  n |= n >> 1
  n |= n >> 2
  n |= n >> 4
  n |= n >> 8
  n |= n >> 16
  n |= n >> 32
  n += 1
  return n


@singledispatch
def cdiv(x: int, y: int):
  return (x + y - 1) // y


@cdiv.register
def cdiv(x: jax.Array, y: int):
  return (x + y - 1) // y


def align_up(x: int, align: int):
  return cdiv(x, align) * align


@singledispatch
def pad_to_multiple(x, multiple: int, axis: int, val):
  raise NotImplementedError(f"pad_to_multiple is not implemented for type {type(x)}")


@pad_to_multiple.register
def pad_to_multiple(x: jax.Array, multiple: int | list, axis: int | list, val):
  if isinstance(multiple, int):
    multiple = [multiple]
  if isinstance(axis, int):
    axis = [axis]

  assert len(multiple) == len(axis), (
    f"Length of multiple {len(multiple)} must match length of axis {len(axis)}"
  )

  shape = list(x.shape)
  pad_width = [(0, 0)] * len(shape)
  for idx in range(0, len(axis)):
    ax = axis[idx]
    mu = multiple[idx]
    length = shape[ax]
    remainder = length % mu
    if remainder == 0:
      continue
    pad_len = mu - remainder
    pad_width[ax] = (0, pad_len)
  return jnp.pad(x, pad_width, constant_values=val)


def pad_to_multiple_varlen(
  x: jax.Array, multiple: int, axis: int, cu_seqlens_cpu: jax.Array
):
  N = len(cu_seqlens_cpu) - 1
  C = multiple
  orig_seqlens = jnp.diff(cu_seqlens_cpu).tolist()
  padded_seqlens = [((L + C - 1) // C) * C for L in orig_seqlens]

  if orig_seqlens == padded_seqlens:
    return x, cu_seqlens_cpu, None, None

  padded = []
  for i in range(N):
    bos = int(cu_seqlens_cpu[i])
    L = orig_seqlens[i]
    pad = padded_seqlens[i] - L
    seg = x[:, bos : bos + L]
    if pad > 0:
      pw = ((0, 0), (0, pad)) + ((0, 0),) * (x.ndim - 2)
      seg = jnp.pad(seg, pw)
    padded.append(seg)

  padded_tensors = jnp.concatenate(padded, axis=1)
  offsets = [0]
  for pl in padded_seqlens:
    offsets.append(offsets[-1] + pl)
  new_cu_seqlens = jnp.array(offsets, dtype=jnp.int32)

  return padded_tensors, new_cu_seqlens, orig_seqlens, padded_seqlens

def segment_ids_to_cu_seqlens(segment_ids) -> jax.Array:
  """Convert sorted segment IDs to cumulative sequence lengths.

  Supports both 0-based and 1-based segment IDs — only transitions
  between adjacent values matter, not the absolute values.

  Args:
      segment_ids: [T] or [B, T] — sorted non-decreasing integer segment IDs.
          E.g. [1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3] for 3 segments of lengths [3, 2, 3].
          When [B, T], each row is processed independently and the results
          are padded to a common N_max+1 length.

  Returns:
      cu_seqlens: [N+1] or [B, N_max+1] int32 — cumulative sequence lengths.
          E.g. [0, 3, 5, 8].
  """
  seg = jnp.asarray(segment_ids)
  if seg.ndim == 1:
    T = seg.shape[0]
    changes = jnp.concatenate([jnp.ones(1, dtype=jnp.bool_), seg[1:] != seg[:-1]])
    n_segs = int(jnp.sum(changes))
    starts = jnp.nonzero(changes, size=n_segs)[0]
    return jnp.concatenate([starts, jnp.array([T])]).astype(jnp.int32)
  # Batched: [B, T]
  assert seg.ndim == 2
  B = seg.shape[0]
  per_batch = [segment_ids_to_cu_seqlens(seg[b]) for b in range(B)]
  n_max = max(cu.shape[0] for cu in per_batch)
  # Pad each to n_max with the last value (total valid length)
  padded = []
  for cu in per_batch:
    pad_len = n_max - cu.shape[0]
    if pad_len > 0:
      padded.append(jnp.concatenate([cu, jnp.full(pad_len, cu[-1], dtype=jnp.int32)]))
    else:
      padded.append(cu)
  return jnp.stack(padded, axis=0)


def prepare_lens(cu_seqlens: jax.Array) -> jax.Array:
  """
  Compute the actual length of each sequence.
  [0, 48, 64] -> [48, 16]
  """
  return cu_seqlens[1:] - cu_seqlens[:-1]


def compute_padded_cu_seqlens(cu_seqlens_cpu: jax.Array, chunk_size: int):
  """Compute padded cumulative sequence lengths.

  Each sequence length is rounded up to the next multiple of
  ``chunk_size``.

  Args:
      cu_seqlens_cpu: [N+1] or [B, N+1] int array — original cumulative
          sequence lengths.
      chunk_size: int — alignment multiple.

  Returns:
      [N+1] or [B, N+1] int array — padded cumulative sequence lengths.
  """
  if cu_seqlens_cpu.ndim == 2:
    # Batched: process each row independently.
    B = cu_seqlens_cpu.shape[0]
    rows = [compute_padded_cu_seqlens(cu_seqlens_cpu[b], chunk_size) for b in range(B)]
    return jnp.stack(rows, axis=0)
  lens = jnp.diff(cu_seqlens_cpu)
  padded_lens = cdiv(lens, chunk_size) * chunk_size
  padded_cu = jnp.concatenate(
    [
      jnp.zeros(1, dtype=cu_seqlens_cpu.dtype),
      jnp.cumsum(padded_lens),
    ]
  )
  return padded_cu


def _merge_short_segments(cu_seqlens, n_segs, min_seg_len, T_in, n_real):
  """Merge segments shorter than min_seg_len, preserving batch boundaries.

  Uses a greedy forward scan: a boundary is kept only if the distance
  from the last accepted boundary is >= ``min_seg_len``, OR the
  boundary falls on a batch element start.

  Args:
      cu_seqlens: [max_segs + 1] initial cu_seqlens.
      n_segs: Number of real segments (traced value).
      min_seg_len: Minimum segment length to keep.
      T_in: Per-batch-element sequence length (for batch boundary detection).
      n_real: Total number of real (non-padding) tokens.

  Returns:
      Filtered cu_seqlens with same shape [max_segs + 1].
  """
  max_segs = cu_seqlens.shape[0] - 1

  def scan_fn(prev_pos, idx):
    cur_pos = cu_seqlens[idx + 1]
    is_real = (idx + 1) <= n_segs
    is_batch_bnd = (cur_pos > 0) & ((cur_pos % T_in) == 0)
    keep = is_real & (((cur_pos - prev_pos) > min_seg_len) | is_batch_bnd)
    new_prev = jnp.where(keep, cur_pos, prev_pos)
    return new_prev, keep

  _, keeps = jax.lax.scan(scan_fn, jnp.int32(0), jnp.arange(max_segs))

  # Compact kept boundaries using cumsum + searchsorted
  kept_cumsum = jnp.cumsum(keeps.astype(jnp.int32))
  n_kept = kept_cumsum[-1]

  query = jnp.arange(1, max_segs + 1, dtype=jnp.int32)
  src_indices = jnp.searchsorted(kept_cumsum, query, side="left")
  src_indices = jnp.clip(src_indices, 0, max_segs - 1)

  out_values = cu_seqlens[src_indices + 1]
  out_values = jnp.where(query <= n_kept, out_values, n_real)

  return jnp.concatenate([jnp.zeros(1, dtype=jnp.int32), out_values])


def align_segment_ids(
  segment_ids: jax.Array,
  N_max: int,
  chunk_size: int,
) -> jax.Array:
  """Align segment_ids to chunk boundaries, matching _align_seqs layout."""
  assert segment_ids.ndim == 1
  assert segment_ids.dtype == jnp.int32
  T = segment_ids.shape[0]

  is_boundary = jnp.concatenate([
    jnp.ones(1, dtype=jnp.bool_),
    segment_ids[1:] != segment_ids[:-1],
  ])
  seg_idx = jnp.cumsum(is_boundary.astype(jnp.int32)) - 1

  positions = jnp.arange(T, dtype=jnp.int32)
  seg_starts = jnp.full(N_max, T, dtype=jnp.int32).at[seg_idx].min(positions)
  seg_ends = jnp.zeros(N_max, dtype=jnp.int32).at[seg_idx].max(positions + 1)
  seg_lens = jnp.maximum(seg_ends - seg_starts, 0)
  seg_labels = segment_ids[jnp.minimum(seg_starts, T - 1)]

  is_real = (seg_labels > 0) & (seg_lens > 0)
  aligned_lens = jnp.where(
    is_real,
    align_up(seg_lens, chunk_size),
    0,
  )
  aligned_starts = jnp.concatenate([
    jnp.zeros(1, dtype=jnp.int32),
    jnp.cumsum(aligned_lens)[:-1],
  ])

  T_aligned = ((T + N_max * (chunk_size - 1) + chunk_size - 1) // chunk_size) * chunk_size
  out = jnp.zeros((T_aligned,), dtype=jnp.int32)
  apos = jnp.arange(T_aligned, dtype=jnp.int32)

  def body(i, ids):
    start = aligned_starts[i]
    end = start + aligned_lens[i]
    mask = is_real[i] & (apos >= start) & (apos < end)
    return jnp.where(mask, seg_labels[i], ids)

  return jax.lax.fori_loop(0, N_max, body, out)


def segment_ids_to_seqlens(
  segment_ids: jax.Array,
  max_segs: int,
  chunk_size: int = 1,
) -> jax.Array:
  """Convert segment_ids to a cu_seqlens boundary array.

  Segment IDs are 1-indexed per-element labels; 0 = padding.  The
  returned array follows the FLA cu_seqlens convention:
  ``cu_seqlens[i]`` is the cumulative end position of segment *i*,
  with phantom (padding) entries beyond the real segment count all
  equal to the total number of valid tokens.

  Args:
      segment_ids: [T] or [B, T] int32 segment IDs (1-indexed; 0 = padding).
          When [B, T], each row is processed independently.
      max_segs: Maximum number of segments (determines output size).
      chunk_size: Chunk size used by the downstream kernel.  Affects
          the ``max_segs`` upper bound.  Defaults to 1 (finest
          granularity, i.e. every position could start a new segment).

  Returns:
      cu_seqlens: [max_segs + 1] or [B, max_segs + 1] int32 array in FLA
          convention ``[0, n1, n1+n2, ...]``.
  """
  if segment_ids.ndim == 2:
    B = segment_ids.shape[0]
    rows = [segment_ids_to_seqlens(segment_ids[b], max_segs, chunk_size) for b in range(B)]
    return jnp.stack(rows, axis=0)
  assert segment_ids.ndim == 1, (
    f"[segment_ids] Expected 1D array [T], got ndim={segment_ids.ndim}"
  )
  assert chunk_size >= 1, f"[chunk_size] Must be >= 1, got {chunk_size}"
  T = segment_ids.shape[0]

  seg = segment_ids.reshape(-1)
  padding_value = 0
  valid = seg != padding_value

  is_boundary = jnp.concatenate([jnp.ones(1, dtype=jnp.bool_), seg[1:] != seg[:-1]])
  is_boundary = is_boundary & valid

  seg_idx = jnp.where(valid, jnp.cumsum(is_boundary.astype(jnp.int32)), padding_value)
  n_segs = seg_idx.max()
  n_real = jnp.sum(valid).astype(jnp.int32)

  is_end = jnp.concatenate([seg[1:] != seg[:-1], jnp.ones(1, dtype=jnp.bool_)]) & valid
  prefix_len = jnp.cumsum(valid.astype(jnp.int32))

  drop_idx = jnp.asarray(max_segs + 1, dtype=jnp.int32)
  scatter_idx = jnp.where(is_end, seg_idx, drop_idx)
  scatter_val = jnp.where(is_end, prefix_len, 0)

  cu_seqlens = jnp.zeros((max_segs + 1,), dtype=jnp.int32)
  cu_seqlens = cu_seqlens.at[scatter_idx].max(scatter_val, mode="drop")

  out_idx = jnp.arange(max_segs + 1, dtype=jnp.int32)
  cu_seqlens = jnp.where(out_idx > n_segs, n_real, cu_seqlens)

  return cu_seqlens


def prepare_chunk_indices(
  cu_seqlens: jax.Array,
  chunk_size: int,
  max_T: int | None = None,
) -> jax.Array:
  """Compute per-chunk (seq_id, block_id) mapping from cu_seqlens.

  Args:
      cu_seqlens: [N+1] or [B, N+1] int array.
      chunk_size: Chunk size.
      max_T: Maximum T for the output. If None, uses cu_seqlens[-1].

  Returns:
      [total_nt, 2] or [B, NT_max, 2] int32 array.
  """
  if cu_seqlens.ndim == 2:
    B = cu_seqlens.shape[0]
    per_batch = [prepare_chunk_indices(cu_seqlens[b], chunk_size,
                                       max_T=max_T) for b in range(B)]
    return jnp.stack(per_batch, axis=0)
  lens = prepare_lens(cu_seqlens)
  n_chunks = cdiv(lens, chunk_size)
  num_seqs = len(lens)
  if max_T is None:
    max_T = cu_seqlens[-1]
  total_nt = max_T // chunk_size
  seq_ids = jnp.repeat(
    jnp.arange(num_seqs, dtype=jnp.int32), n_chunks, total_repeat_length=total_nt
  )
  prefix_chunks = jnp.concatenate([jnp.zeros(1, dtype=jnp.int32), jnp.cumsum(n_chunks)])
  seq_offsets = jnp.repeat(prefix_chunks[:-1], n_chunks, total_repeat_length=total_nt)
  block_ids = jnp.arange(total_nt, dtype=jnp.int32) - seq_offsets
  return jnp.stack([seq_ids, block_ids], axis=1)


def assert_shape_or_none(
  x: jax.Array | list[jax.Array | None] | tuple[jax.Array | None, ...] | None,
  expected_shape: list[int] | tuple[int, ...],
  name: str | list[str] | tuple[str, ...] = "tensor",
):
  """
  Concise helper to assert tensor shapes.
  Skips assertion for any element that is None.
  Supports a single array or an iterable of arrays that should all match the expected shape.
  """
  if x is None:
    return

  if isinstance(x, (list, tuple)):
    has_names = isinstance(name, (list, tuple)) and len(name) == len(x)
    for i, tensor in enumerate(x):
      if tensor is not None:
        curr_name = name[i] if has_names else f"{name}_{i}"
        assert tensor.shape == expected_shape, (
          f"[{curr_name}] Expected shape {expected_shape}, got {tensor.shape}"
        )
  else:
    assert x.shape == expected_shape, (
      f"[{name}] Expected shape {expected_shape}, got {x.shape}"
    )


def assert_shape(
  x: jax.Array | list[jax.Array] | tuple[jax.Array, ...],
  expected_shape: list[int] | tuple[int, ...],
  name: str | list[str] | tuple[str, ...] = "tensor",
):
  """
  Concise helper to assert tensor shapes.
  Supports a single array or an iterable of arrays that should all match the expected shape.
  """
  if isinstance(x, (list, tuple)):
    # If name is not a sequence or has mismatched length, use a generic numbered name
    has_names = isinstance(name, (list, tuple)) and len(name) == len(x)
    for i, tensor in enumerate(x):
      curr_name = name[i] if has_names else f"{name}_{i}"
      assert tensor.shape == expected_shape, (
        f"[{curr_name}] Expected shape {expected_shape}, got {tensor.shape}"
      )
  else:
    assert x.shape == expected_shape, (
      f"[{name}] Expected shape {expected_shape}, got {x.shape}"
    )


def export_public(current_globals):
  """ """
  public_members = []

  module_name = current_globals.get("__name__")

  for name, obj in current_globals.items():
    if name.startswith("_"):
      continue

    if hasattr(obj, "__module__") and obj.__module__ != module_name:
      continue

    if isinstance(obj, types.ModuleType):
      continue

    if name == "export_public":
      continue

    public_members.append(name)

  return public_members
